research: Line: slate Miami -34.5; archive open -33.5, close -32.5 (DraftKings via ESPN). The close is 2 points under the slate, so the slate number is the high end of the range and the edge has to be judged at 32.5. [spread] (helps North Alabama at the slate number only)

Predictem (Nov 13): Barttorvik adjusted ratings plus home court put Miami's margin in the mid-to-high 20s. The writer notes early ratings still lean on preseason priors. [spread] (helps North Alabama)

Predictem (Nov 13): Miami is 14 of 63 from three on the season (about 22%) and has never made more than five threes in a game. A 33+ margin has to come from the paint and transition. [angle] (helps North Alabama)

Predictem (Nov 13): North Alabama lost only 81-72 at Oklahoma on Monday, trailing 37-36 at halftime, and Oklahoma needed 13 threes. That is a road result against an SEC team. [angle] (helps North Alabama)

Predictem (Nov 13): Mike Evbagharu averages 19 points and 7 rebounds and went 10 of 11 for 27 at Oklahoma, and Quan Lax scored 19 and 14. North Alabama has a scoring answer inside. (helps North Alabama)

Predictem (Nov 13): North Alabama committed 19 turnovers at UC Davis and gave up 10 offensive rebounds to Oklahoma. Miami forced 15 and 17 turnovers and grabbed 23 offensive rebounds vs North Florida, which is a blowout path. [angle] (helps Miami)

No ATS records or injury news were found in a pre-game source. With one clean preview, this is fewer independent sources than I'd like. (neutral)
games.reasoning: Efficiency models put Miami's margin in the high 20s, but buy-game markets sit above those numbers routinely, and the close (-32.5) is near my 31. The most interesting angle is Miami's broken three-point shooting, which limits how fast it can run up a 33-point margin. Against the close the gap is only 1.5, so I pass. A Miami lineup absence or a hot shooting history would have changed it.
